by_task.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable and the asset is a motor vehicle.
by_task.procedure: Apply Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g) as a separate motor-vehicle alternative. Start with its $4,000 ceiling and add the unused amount of the $12,000 § 815.18(3)(d) allowance; under independent asset-exemption evaluation, no other listed asset consumes that allowance. For one debtor, report the lesser of the whole vehicle's value and $16,000.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not stop at $4,000 when the unused consumer-goods allowance raises the motor-vehicle ceiling, and do not add § 815.18(3)(d) to the vehicle merely because it is tangible personal property.

by_task.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable and the asset is a motor vehicle.
by_task.procedure: Apply Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g) separately. Under independent asset-exemption evaluation, its $4,000 ceiling receives the unused $12,000 § 815.18(3)(d) allowance, yielding $16,000 per debtor. Report the lesser of whole-vehicle value and $16,000 for one debtor; for two equal joint debtors, apply § 815.18(8) to each half and sum the protected interests, up to $32,000 for the whole vehicle.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not stop at $4,000, leave joint debtors at one debtor's $16,000 ceiling, or add § 815.18(3)(d) as a separate vehicle citation merely because the vehicle is tangible personal property.
